title: Let's get to know your money
intro: A few quick questions to set your first goal. There are no right answers, and you can skip anytime.

skip.label: Skip for now
skip.confirm: No problem. You'll start from the beginning with a default goal of {goal}, about one month of typical essentials. You can personalize anytime in Settings.

resultSkipped: Your first loaf: Emergency fund. Starting goal: {goal}, a default you can change in Settings.
personalizePrompt: Answer a few quick questions for a personalized pick

result.title: Here's where you'll start
result.goalMonths: Goal: {goal}, about {months} of your monthly essentials.
result.goalDefault: Goal: {goal}, a starter goal you can change anytime. It isn't a guess at what you spend.
result.headStart: Head start: the {saved} you already have set aside puts you {percent}% of the way there.
result.noHeadStart: You're starting from a dough ball, and that's a fine place to start.
result.investmentNote: You already invest, which is great. A cushion means you never have to sell investments at a loss when something urgent comes up.
result.baked: Your emergency fund is already built. Nice work. It goes on your bread shelf as "Already built."

newLoaf.title: Your new loaf
newLoaf.starterNote: {goal} is a starter goal because we don't know your monthly essentials yet. It isn't an estimate of what you spend. You can change it here or in Settings.
newLoaf.needsExact: Your essentials are in the top range. Type your exact monthly amount to size your goal. This is optional.
newLoaf.countSavings: Count the money I already have set aside
newLoaf.biggerTarget: Your savings already cover this goal. Pick a bigger one so you have something to build toward.
newLoaf.builtTitle: Your emergency fund is already built
newLoaf.builtBody: You've set aside enough to cover your goal, so this loaf goes straight to your shelf. Want to see what you've built, or move on?

questions.prompt: About how much do you need each month to cover your essentials?
questions.help: Rent, food, phone, transportation, and anything else you'd need to get by for a month. If your housing or meals are prepaid, count only what you still pay each month.

questions.prompt: How much money do you already have set aside for emergencies?
questions.help: Money you'd reach for if something urgent came up. Leave out money you've set aside for rent, tuition, or other planned costs.

questions.prompt: Which of these accounts do you have?
questions.help: Choose all that apply. This helps us skip steps you've already done.

questions.prompt: Do you carry a credit card balance from month to month?
questions.help: Carrying a balance means you don't pay the full amount by the due date, so interest gets added.

options.label: I don't have a credit card

questions.prompt: Do you earn income from a job?
questions.help: Part-time, full-time, work-study, or gig work all count.
